title: Stacks
summary: Last in, first out: match brackets and build undo with a stack.

steps.title: Last in, first out
body: A **stack** is a pile of plates: you only touch the top. `Push` puts an item on top, `Pop` takes the top one off, `Peek` looks at it without removing it. All three are `O(1)`.
stack.Pop();   // 2: the last one in is the first one out
Under the hood `Stack<T>` is just a dynamic array where the top is the end. Watch the array version below: `top` moves up on push and down on pop.

steps.explain: Pop `b`, push `c` and `d`, pop `d` then `c`. `Peek` shows `a` without removing it.

steps.title: Balanced brackets
body: Is `([]{})` properly nested? Read left to right:
- a **closing** bracket must match the opener on top, which is popped,
- at the end the stack must be empty.
The stack remembers *which openers are still waiting*, most recent on top. Watch it grow and shrink in the trace.

code: if (stack.Count == 0 || stack.Pop() != want) { ok = false; break; }

steps.prompt: Checking `([)]`: after reading `(` and `[`, the next character is `)`. What happens?
options: The top is `[`, which does not match `)`, so the text is unbalanced
`(` is found lower in the stack, so it matches
The stack is empty, so it is unbalanced
steps.explain: A closer must match the **most recent** unmatched opener. `[` is on top, so `)` arrives too early.

steps.prompt: Complete the bracket check for round brackets only.
steps.explain: With one kind of bracket the stack only ever holds `(`, so a counter is enough. Going below zero means a `)` with nothing to close.

steps.prompt: Does each job want a stack (last in, first out) or a queue (first in, first out)?
items: matching HTML open and close tags
messages processed in the order they arrived

steps.title: Every kind of bracket
prompt: Write `bool Balanced(string s)` for `()`, `[]` and `{}`. Ignore every other character.
template: Dojo.Eq("\"{ a[1] + (b) }\" is balanced", true, Balanced("{ a[1] + (b) }"));
Dojo.Eq("an empty string is balanced", true, Balanced(""));
hints: Push openers. For a closer, work out which opener it needs.
If the stack is empty or the popped opener is the wrong one, return false. At the end, return `stack.Count == 0`.

steps.title: Undo
prompt: Build a tiny editor with undo. Write a class `Editor`:
- `string Text` (property): the current text, starting empty.
- `void Backspace()`: deletes the last character (does nothing when empty).
- `bool Undo()`: reverts the most recent `Type` or `Backspace` that is not yet undone and returns `true`; returns `false` when there is nothing to undo.
Use a `Stack<string>` of earlier texts: before each change, push the current text.
starter: public string Text { get; private set; } = "";
solution: public string Text { get; private set; } = "";
template: Dojo.Eq("Undo with no history returns false", false, dojoE.Undo());
Dojo.Eq("Backspace removes the last character", "Hello wor", dojoE.Text);
Dojo.Eq("Undo reverts one backspace", "Hello worl", dojoE.Text);
Dojo.Eq("undoing a Type removes the whole word", "Hello", dojoE.Text);
Dojo.Eq("Backspace on empty text is not recorded", false, dojoE.Undo());
hints: `Undo`: if the stack is empty return false; otherwise `Text = history.Pop();`. `Text[..^1]` drops the last character.
